title: Moving his mother and sister's children to Jamaica, Long Island
summary: He bought a house for his mother and the children in Jamaica, coming through Philadelphia first because it was cheaper, on Nazarro's $90-a-week pay scale.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: George what I want to tell you about was I think everyone is concerned with their mother and father. I think I told you about having to go back to New York -- to go back to Louisville from New York, my first trip when my father died. I'm sure I told you that, didn't I? Remember that?

Okay, now I want to tell you about where my mother was in New York during the time I'm doing all other things. I get a house for my mother with the children she had to contend with in Jamaica, Long Island, because it was a good place, they got a yard for children to play in and everything and it's away from the intermediate traffic. You don't have to worry about children going across the street or on the street and it's home-like style. I got her there but I had to

go far away. See I was only getting $100 a week when I first began to go to New York with Nazarro, changing from $35 a week for each mother for us, for Buck and I. Nazarro was going to give us $100 a week -- or rather, $90 a week for the first three years -- beg your pardon. It was $90 for the first year, $100 a week for the second year and $100 a week for the third year and for the fourth year $125.

Before we get to New York on this contract -- my mother and these kids are in Jamaica now -- I had to go by the way of Philadelphia because Philadelphia is a cheaper place to live than New York. So I take my mother, my niece and my sister by way of Philadelphia coming into New York and I got them a place to live in Philadelphia for a couple of months while I get some more money together so they could come into New York.
